title: Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management: generative insights in Demand planning, with a trends metric at general availability
summary: The briefing passes: the roadmap targets, automatic availability, licensing requirements and both control rows are supported. Minor corrections should name the licence-assignment request properties, complete two abbreviated control routes and correct the attribution of the user-access requirement.

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: The roadmap plans a new trends metric at general availability.

claims.claim: The planned trends metric dynamically clusters data into detected patterns including high trending, medium trending, relative flat and declining trend.
claims.quote: The system dynamically clusters data based on detected patterns, such as high trending, medium trending, relative flat, and declining trend.

claims.claim: Planners can view aggregated values by selected dimensions.
claims.quote: You can view aggregated values by selected dimensions or drill down into detailed values for each planning object.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn describes generative insights as a production-ready preview.
claims.quote: [This article is prerelease documentation and is subject to change.] ... This is a production-ready preview feature.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support; Scope: When
claims.claim: The feature page currently documents seasonality and signal correlation as its two metrics.
claims.quote: It currently supports two metrics: seasonality and signal correlation.

claims.claim: The feature page does not mention trends.
claims.quote: Searched: read the complete generative-insights feature page for trends; it names seasonality and signal correlation but contains no trends metric.

claims.claim: A planner can open a time series through Planning data > Forecasts in Demand planning.
claims.quote: Open the time series that you want to analyze. For example, on the navigation pane, select Planning data > Forecasts, and then select a time series.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Selecting Generate insights runs the AI model on the current time series.
claims.quote: If you've never generated insights for the current time series, then select the Generate insights button available here. The system then runs the AI model to generate insights for the current time series.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: The preview presents confidence scores for detected insights.
claims.quote: A confidence score that indicates how confident the system is about each detected insight.

claims.claim: The preview presents relevant key figures for each insight.
claims.quote: Various relevant KPI values for each insight.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: The preview presents natural-language descriptions of insights for planners to read.
claims.quote: A description of each insight, which is written in natural language. This description typically explains the detected pattern and its significance.

claims.claim: The preview presents graphs of relevant insight data.
claims.quote: Several graphs of relevant data, with tabs that organize the data by insight type (Signal correlation and Seasonality).

claims.claim: Detailed insight graphs can identify contributors by dimension, such as products or locations.
claims.quote: Some detailed graphs provide a dimension breakdown that lets you review the major contributors to the detected insights. For example, you can see which products or locations contributed most to the detected seasonality or signal correlation.

claims.claim: Production-ready previews are subject to supplemental terms of use.
claims.quote: Production-ready previews are subject to supplemental terms of use.

claims.where: Why it matters; Governance guidance: Before rollout

claims.quote: AI-generated content should not be used without manual review or supervision.

claims.claim: The FAQ recommends controlling data permissions to prevent manipulation of business data that undesirably influences AI processing.
claims.quote: Make sure that your company has enough control over data permissions to ensure that business data can't be manipulated to influence AI data processing in an undesirable way.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: The FAQ advises reviewing the generated response and comparing it with actual demand plan data before deciding to modify a plan.
claims.quote: Before you make decisions about modifying a demand plan, always review and study the generated response, and compare it with actual demand plan data.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model and notes; Cost and licensing; Scope: Prerequisites; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Demand planning requires a licence for each relevant user in production, supporting the per-user licensing model.
claims.quote: To use Demand planning in Microsoft Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management in a production environment, each relevant user must have a license for it.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: An administrator must assign a purchased Demand planning licence to each user who needs it.
claims.quote: After purchasing the required licenses, an administrator must assign one to each user that needs it.

claims.claim: The licensing page directs readers to Supply Chain Management pricing and the Dynamics 365 Licensing Guide for plans, prices and licensing details.
claims.quote: For an overview of Supply Chain Management and Demand planning licensing plans and prices, see Supply Chain Management pricing. ... For complete licensing details ... see the Dynamics 365 Licensing Guide.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: A licence specific to generative insights is not yet published.
claims.quote: Searched: "generative insights" "Demand planning" license pricing Copilot Credits; opened generative-insights, demand-planning-licensing and Supply Chain Management pricing. No feature-specific licence found; the product per-user requirement is published.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: A meter specific to generative insights is not yet published.
claims.quote: Searched: "generative insights" "Demand planning" license pricing Copilot Credits; read licensing, feature and pricing pages and billing-rate search excerpts. Pricing requires credits for agents; no passage identifies generative insights as an agent or meters this feature.

claims.claim: The Demand planning licensing page mentions neither generative insights nor Copilot Credits.
claims.quote: Searched: read the complete demand-planning-licensing page for generative insights and Copilot Credits; neither is present.

claims.claim: The generative insights feature page names no licence.
claims.quote: Searched: read the complete generative-insights feature page for licence and license requirements; none is named. The page separately states supplemental preview terms.

claims.where: Scope: Who; Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: Demand planning users need a Power Platform account with the security roles for the features they use, attributed in Scope to the install page.
claims.quote: To be able to access Demand planning, users must sign in a Power Platform user account that has the security roles for the features they need.
claims.fix: In Scope: Who, replace 'the install page says users need the Power Platform roles for the features they use' with 'the security roles page says users need a Power Platform account with the security roles for the features they need'. The cited users-access page, not the install page, states this.

claims.where: Scope: Who; Risk assessment: Security & identity; controls[1].note
claims.claim: Demand Planning Contributor grants access to Demand planning, worksheet viewing and editing of accessible data.
claims.quote: Demand Planning Contributor ... Grants access to Demand planing. ... View worksheets (see shared worksheets and save their own views). ... Controlled by row-level access and can edit data they have access to.

claims.where: Scope: Who; Risk assessment: Security & identity; controls[1].note
claims.claim: Demand Planning Manager grants access to Demand planning and the Contributor features.
claims.quote: Demand Planning Manager ... Grants access to Demand planning and all features that are available to the Demand Planning Contributor role.

claims.where: Scope: Who; Risk assessment: Security & identity; controls[1].note
claims.claim: System Administrator grants access to Demand planning and its admin features.
claims.quote: System Administrator ... Grants access to Demand planning and all features that are available to the Demand Planning Manager, Demand Planning Contributor, and Basic User roles. ... Grants access to admin features within Demand planning.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Scope: Who
claims.claim: Contributors who do not also hold Demand Planning Manager or System Administrator can view and edit only data granted by row-level access rules.
claims.quote: Users who have the Demand Planning Contributor role (but not Demand Planning Manager or System Administrator) ... can only view and edit data that they're granted access to. You control this access using row-level security, which is set up in Demand planning.

claims.claim: The generative insights feature page does not describe whether generated insights are limited to the user's permitted rows.
claims.quote: Searched: "generative insights" "row-level" Demand planning security; read feature, FAQ and users-access pages. General Contributor row-level security is documented, but the feature page does not describe filtering of generated insights.

claims.claim: Demand planning is installed as a Power Platform app through the Power Platform admin center.
claims.quote: Install Demand planning in Power Platform admin center ... Select Resources > Dynamics 365 apps ... Search for and select the app named Dynamics 365 Demand Planning Application. ... Select Install.

claims.claim: Demand planning can be linked to Supply Chain Management.
claims.quote: Go to System administration > Setup > Demand planning app parameters. ... On the General tab, in the Demand planning app URL field, enter the URL where Demand planning is installed.

claims.claim: Using Demand planning with Supply Chain Management requires installing and enabling Demand planning.
claims.quote: It explains how to use Power Platform admin center to install Demand planning in your tenant and set up the feature in Supply Chain Management. ... In the Feature management workspace, turn on the Demand Planning feature.

claims.claim: The Demand Planning feature in Feature management is on by default as of Supply Chain Management version 10.0.40.
claims.quote: In the Feature management workspace, turn on the Demand Planning feature. (As of Supply Chain Management version 10.0.40, it's turned on by default.)

claims.claim: The finance and operations Copilot enablement page lists no setting specific to generative insights.
claims.quote: Searched: "generative insights" "Demand planning" disable setting Feature management; read enable-copilot and feature pages. The table says automatically installed and enabled; Publish bots with AI features is general. Analyze demand plans with Copilot is a different feature.

claims.where: summary; Why it matters; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Publish bots with AI features is a tenant-level control for Copilot features in finance and operations apps.
claims.quote: By default, the tenant-level setting that enables the deployment of Copilot bots in Dataverse environments is enabled. ... If the setting is disabled, you can't use Copilot features in finance and operations apps.

claims.claim: Publish bots with AI features is enabled by default.
claims.quote: By default, the tenant-level setting that enables the deployment of Copilot bots in Dataverse environments is enabled.

claims.claim: A tenant admin can disable the Publish bots with AI features setting.
claims.quote: However, a tenant admin can disable this setting.

claims.claim: Disabling the tenant-level AI setting prevents use of Copilot features in finance and operations apps.
claims.quote: If the setting is disabled, you can't use Copilot features in finance and operations apps.

claims.claim: Generative insights is automatically installed and enabled when Demand planning is installed.
claims.quote: Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management | Generative insights for Demand planning | Automatically installed and enabled when you install Demand planning.

claims.claim: The tenant AI setting is under Settings in the Power Platform admin center.
claims.quote: On the navigation pane, select Settings. ... select the row where the Name field is set to Publish bots with AI features. ... In the Publish Copilots with AI features dialog box, set the option to Enabled or Disabled, as you prefer.
claims.fix: Replace '(Power Platform admin center, Settings)' with '(Power Platform admin center, Settings > Publish bots with AI features > Publish Copilots with AI features > Enabled or Disabled)', as documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/dynamics365/fin-ops-core/dev-itpro/copilot/enable-copilot.

claims.where: Governance controls: Demand Planning feature switch
claims.claim: Learn does not state whether the Supply Chain Management Demand Planning feature switch governs generative insights.
claims.quote: Searched: "generative insights" "Demand planning" disable setting Feature management; read install-demand-planning, enable-copilot and generative-insights. The switch enables Demand planning in Supply Chain Management; no explicit effect on generated insights is stated.

claims.claim: POST /v1.0/users/{id | userPrincipalName}/assignLicense assigns or removes user licences.
